CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
Region is Dompu Regency. 1. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of Regional autonomy. 2. Regent is the Regent of Dompu. 3. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Dompu Regency. 4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the region. 5. Office hereinafter referred to as PPPA Office is the Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Dompu Regency. 6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old, including a child who is still in the womb. 7. Woman is a person who is female in gender. 8. Violence is any act against the physical and psychological aspects that is unlawful, with or without using means, that endangers life or the body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 9. Violence Against Women is any Action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, or psychologically, economic exploitation, social, including threats of certain Actions, coercion, or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 10. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, social, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 11. Domestic violence is any Action or act against a person especially women that results in misery or neglect of the household including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 12. Criminal Act of Sexual Violence hereinafter abbreviated as TPKS is any act that meets the elements of a criminal act as regulated in the Law on Criminal Acts of Sexual Violence and other sexual acts regulated in the Law as long as determined in the Law on Criminal Acts of Sexual Violence. 13. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecution, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 14. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 16. Companion is a person or representative from an Institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy, advocacy, reintegration for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 17. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering either physical, mental or emotional, economic loss either physical suffering, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights as a result of human rights violations or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or individuals including the victim's heirs. 18. Prevention is an effort made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 19. Outreach is an action to respond to reports of alleged problems of women and children that need to be verified and followed up. 20. Social rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to be able to carry out social functions properly in community life. 21. Coordination is an effort made to realize integration and harmony in the context of services for women and children experiencing problems. 22. Task Force for Handling Women's and Children's Problems hereinafter abbreviated as Satgas PPA is a task force formed to handle women's and children's problems reported to women's and children's service organizations that have been established by the regional government. 23. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Women's and Children's Protection hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a Regional Technical Implementation Unit established by the Regional Government in providing Services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems. 24. Regional Child Protection Commission hereinafter abbreviated as KPAD is an independent Institution established by the Regent to support supervision of the implementation of child protection in the region. 25. Integrated Community-Based Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as PATBM is a movement of networks or groups of citizens at the community level who work in a coordinated manner to achieve the goals of child protection. 26. Regional Long-Term Development Plan hereinafter referred to as RPJPD is a regional planning document for a period of 20 (twenty) years. 27. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan hereinafter referred to as RPJMD is a regional planning document for a period of 5 (five) years. 28. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Human Trafficking is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating efforts to prevent and handle criminal acts of human trafficking in Dompu Regency. 29. Task Force for Prevention of Child Marriage is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating efforts to prevent child marriage in Dompu Regency. 30.

Article 11
Other violence as referred to in Article 5 (1) letter g, constitutes threat of violence and coercion. Threat of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) includes every unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, image, symbol, or body movement, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
Coercion as referred to in paragraph (1) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 6
(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 5 letter a, constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or causes death of Women and/or Children.
(2) Physical violence as referred to in paragraph (1) results in: the victim suffering from serious illness or injury;
a. death of the victim; and/or
b. causing illness or impediment to carrying out work duties or livelihood or daily activities.

Article 8
Paragraph (2) Letter h
What is meant by sexual violence in the household is any act in the form of forced sexual relations, forced sexual relations in an unnatural and/or undesired manner, forced sexual relations with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Article 37
The Regional Government may provide assistance to women and children victims of violence.
Assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) includes all integrated efforts to restore and strengthen the condition of victims, which are carried out at health service units, education, the police, the prosecutor's office, the courts, and social service institutions.
Assistance as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out by UPTD PPA assistants and other assistants.

Article 56
(1) Regional Government may establish partnerships with the Business Sector in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are conducted through:
a. notification of employment opportunity information for Women and Child Victims of Acts of Violence, and
b. education and training for Women and Child Victims of Acts of Violence.

CHAPTER IV
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Article 16
The Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Acts of Violence is a joint obligation and responsibility of:
a. Regional Government;
b. Private Sector and Community Institutions;
c. Society; and
d. Family and/or Parents.

Article 20
The Obligations of Family and/or Parents as referred to in Article 16 letter d, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as Family members.

I. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural, and the social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as an integral part of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens through various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women’s empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected that they will be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen forms of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.
Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, the community, and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when there is potential violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The said efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.
In connection with the aforementioned matters, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as to ensure legal certainty in the implementation of women’s empowerment and the protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

(1) Special Protection for Child Victims of Physical and/or Psychological Violence as referred to in Article 38 paragraph (2) letter i, is carried out through efforts to:
a. disseminate and socialize the provisions of laws and regulations that protect Child victims of acts of violence; and
b. monitor, report, and impose sanctions.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
Region is Dompu Regency. 1. Office hereinafter referred to as PPPA Office is the Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Dompu Regency. 6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old, including a child who is still in the womb. 7. Woman is a person who is female in gender. 8. Violence is any act against the physical and psychological aspects that is unlawful, with or without using means, that endangers life or the body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 9. Violence Against Women is any Action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, or psychologically, economic exploitation, social, including threats of certain Actions, coercion, or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 10. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, social, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 11. Domestic violence is any Action or act against a person especially women that results in misery or neglect of the household including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 12. Criminal Act of Sexual Violence hereinafter abbreviated as TPKS is any act that meets the elements of a criminal act as regulated in the Law on Criminal Acts of Sexual Violence and other sexual acts regulated in the Law as long as determined in the Law on Criminal Acts of Sexual Violence. 13. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecution, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 14. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 16. Companion is a person or representative from an Institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy, advocacy, reintegration for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 17. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering either physical, mental or emotional, economic loss either physical suffering, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights as a result of human rights violations or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or individuals including the victim's heirs. 18. Prevention is an effort made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 19. Outreach is an action to respond to reports of alleged problems of women and children that need to be verified and followed up. 20. Social rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to be able to carry out social functions properly in community life. 21. Coordination is an effort made to realize integration and harmony in the context of services for women and children experiencing problems. 22. Task Force for Handling Women's and Children's Problems hereinafter abbreviated as Satgas PPA is a task force formed to handle women's and children's problems reported to women's and children's service organizations that have been established by the regional government. 23. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Women's and Children's Protection hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a Regional Technical Implementation Unit established by the Regional Government in providing Services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems. 24. Regional Child Protection Commission hereinafter abbreviated as KPAD is an independent Institution established by the Regent to support supervision of the implementation of child protection in the region. 25. Integrated Community-Based Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as PATBM is a movement of networks or groups of citizens at the community level who work in a coordinated manner to achieve the goals of child protection. 26. Regional Long-Term Development Plan hereinafter referred to as RPJPD is a regional planning document for a period of 20 (twenty) years. 27. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan hereinafter referred to as RPJMD is a regional planning document for a period of 5 (five) years. 28. Article 6
(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 5 letter a, constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or causes death of Women and/or Children.
(2) Physical violence as referred to in paragraph (1) results in: the victim suffering from serious illness or injury;
a. death of the victim; and/or
b. causing illness or impediment to carrying out work duties or livelihood or daily activities.

Article 8
Paragraph (2) Letter h
What is meant by sexual violence in the household is any act in the form of forced sexual relations, forced sexual relations in an unnatural and/or undesired manner, forced sexual relations with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Article 11
Other violence as referred to in Article 5 (1) letter g, constitutes threat of violence and coercion. Threat of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) includes every unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, image, symbol, or body movement, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
Coercion as referred to in paragraph (1) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 10
(1) Exploitation as referred to in Article 5 letter e, includes:
a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, physical exploitation, sexual exploitation, exploitation of reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or capabilities of a person by other parties to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. acts of exploiting children in horse racing activities as jockeys by disregarding the rights of children and/or with the intention of exploiting the labor or capabilities of children to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
(2) The involvement of children in horse racing activities as jockeys as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, shall be further regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 20
The Obligations of Family and/or Parents as referred to in Article 16 letter d, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as Family members.

Article 7
Psychological violence as referred to in Article 5 letter b, constitutes acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering to Women and/or Children.

I. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural, and the social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as an integral part of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens through various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women’s empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected that they will be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen forms of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.
Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, the community, and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when there is potential violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The said efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.
In connection with the aforementioned matters, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as to ensure legal certainty in the implementation of women’s empowerment and the protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER IV
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Article 16
The Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Acts of Violence is a joint obligation and responsibility of:
a. Regional Government;
b. Private Sector and Community Institutions;
c. Society; and
d. Family and/or Parents.

Article 56
(1) Regional Government may establish partnerships with the Business Sector in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are conducted through:
a. notification of employment opportunity information for Women and Child Victims of Acts of Violence, and
b. education and training for Women and Child Victims of Acts of Violence.

I. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural, and the social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as an integral part of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens through various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women’s empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected that they will be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen forms of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.
Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, the community, and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when there is potential violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The said efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.
In connection with the aforementioned matters, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as to ensure legal certainty in the implementation of women’s empowerment and the protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as an integral part of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens through various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women’s empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected that they will be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen forms of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.
Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, the community, and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when there is potential violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The said efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.
In connection with the aforementioned matters, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as to ensure legal certainty in the implementation of women’s empowerment and the protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
Region is Dompu Regency. 1. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of Regional autonomy. 2. Regent is the Regent of Dompu. 3. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Dompu Regency. 4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the region. 5. Office hereinafter referred to as PPPA Office is the Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Dompu Regency. 6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old, including a child who is still in the womb. 7. Woman is a person who is female in gender. 8. Violence is any act against the physical and psychological aspects that is unlawful, with or without using means, that endangers life or the body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 9. Violence Against Women is any Action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, or psychologically, economic exploitation, social, including threats of certain Actions, coercion, or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 10. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, social, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 11. Domestic violence is any Action or act against a person especially women that results in misery or neglect of the household including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 12. Criminal Act of Sexual Violence hereinafter abbreviated as TPKS is any act that meets the elements of a criminal act as regulated in the Law on Criminal Acts of Sexual Violence and other sexual acts regulated in the Law as long as determined in the Law on Criminal Acts of Sexual Violence. 13. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecution, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 14. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 16. Companion is a person or representative from an Institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy, advocacy, reintegration for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 17. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering either physical, mental or emotional, economic loss either physical suffering, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights as a result of human rights violations or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or individuals including the victim's heirs. 18. Outreach is an action to respond to reports of alleged problems of women and children that need to be verified and followed up. 20. Social rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to be able to carry out social functions properly in community life. 21. Coordination is an effort made to realize integration and harmony in the context of services for women and children experiencing problems. 22. Task Force for Handling Women's and Children's Problems hereinafter abbreviated as Satgas PPA is a task force formed to handle women's and children's problems reported to women's and children's service organizations that have been established by the regional government. 23. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Women's and Children's Protection hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a Regional Technical Implementation Unit established by the Regional Government in providing Services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems. 24. Regional Child Protection Commission hereinafter abbreviated as KPAD is an independent Institution established by the Regent to support supervision of the implementation of child protection in the region. 25. Integrated Community-Based Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as PATBM is a movement of networks or groups of citizens at the community level who work in a coordinated manner to achieve the goals of child protection. 26. Regional Long-Term Development Plan hereinafter referred to as RPJPD is a regional planning document for a period of 20 (twenty) years. 27. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan hereinafter referred to as RPJMD is a regional planning document for a period of 5 (five) years. 28. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Human Trafficking is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating efforts to prevent and handle criminal acts of human trafficking in Dompu Regency. 29. Task Force for Prevention of Child Marriage is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating efforts to prevent child marriage in Dompu Regency. 30.

Article 33
(1) Repatriation and social reintegration services as referred to in Article 28 paragraph (1) letter e, aim to return victims to be accepted back into their social environment.
(2) Repatriation and social reintegration services for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out after socialization related to the rights of women and children as victims of violence.
(3) Repatriation and social reintegration services as referred to in paragraph (2) are carried out by the Regional Government in coordination with regional apparatus/related institutions, and the community.

Article 31
(1) Legal aid services as referred to in Article 28 paragraph (1) letter c, aim to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process.

b. accompanying victims at the reporting, investigation, prosecution, and examination levels in court hearings and assisting victims to comprehensively describe the violence they have experienced; and
c. coordinating with fellow law enforcers, volunteer companions, and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

The Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Acts of Violence is a joint obligation and responsibility of:
a. Regional Government;
b. Private Sector and Community Institutions;
c. Society; and
d. Family and/or Parents.

I. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural, and the social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as an integral part of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens through various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women’s empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected that they will be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen forms of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.
Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, the community, and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when there is potential violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The said efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.
In connection with the aforementioned matters, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as to ensure legal certainty in the implementation of women’s empowerment and the protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural, and the social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as an integral part of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens through various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women’s empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected that they will be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen forms of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.
Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, the community, and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when there is potential violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The said efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.
In connection with the aforementioned matters, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as to ensure legal certainty in the implementation of women’s empowerment and the protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

Fourth Part
Assistance

I. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural, and the social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as an integral part of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens through various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women’s empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected that they will be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen forms of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.
Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, the community, and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when there is potential violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The said efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.
In connection with the aforementioned matters, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as to ensure legal certainty in the implementation of women’s empowerment and the protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

CHAPTER IV
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Article 16
The Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Acts of Violence is a joint obligation and responsibility of:
a. Regional Government;
b. Private Sector and Community Institutions;
c. Society; and
d. Family and/or Parents.

I. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural, and the social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as an integral part of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens through various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women’s empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected that they will be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen forms of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.
Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, the community, and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when there is potential violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The said efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.
In connection with the aforementioned matters, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as to ensure legal certainty in the implementation of women’s empowerment and the protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

Article 25
(1) The Regional Government may establish a PPA Task Force in an effort to coordinate the provision of services for Women and Children who are victims of acts of violence.
(2) The PPA Task Force as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to:
   a. coordinate and synchronize protection services for women and children carried out by the Regional Government, Regional Apparatus/Institutions, and the community;
   b. improve cooperation and referral systems; and collect, compile, and present reports on violence.
(3) The establishment of the PPA Task Force as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be stipulated by Regent's Decree.

Article 31
(1) Legal aid services as referred to in Article 28 paragraph (1) letter c, aim to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process.
(2) Legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by:
a. providing legal consultation that includes information regarding victims' rights and the judicial process;
b. accompanying victims at the reporting, investigation, prosecution, and examination levels in court hearings and assisting victims to comprehensively describe the violence they have experienced; and
c. coordinating with fellow law enforcers, volunteer companions, and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

Article 15
The safe house as referred to in Article 14 paragraph (1) provides a place and/or temporary safe shelter for victims of violence.
The organization and/or management of the safe house (2) as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the PPPA Office.
(3) For security and at the request of the victim of violence, the manager or organizer of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (2) may place the victim of violence in a certain place that is kept confidential.
(4) Provisions regarding the organizer of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (2) are further regulated in the Regent Regulation.

I. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural, and the social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as an integral part of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens through various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women’s empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected that they will be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen forms of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.
Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, the community, and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when there is potential violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The said efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.
In connection with the aforementioned matters, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as to ensure legal certainty in the implementation of women’s empowerment and the protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural, and the social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as an integral part of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens through various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women’s empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected that they will be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen forms of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.
Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, the community, and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when there is potential violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The said efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.
In connection with the aforementioned matters, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as to ensure legal certainty in the implementation of women’s empowerment and the protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural, and the social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as an integral part of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens through various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women’s empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected that they will be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen forms of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.
Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, the community, and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when there is potential violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The said efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.
In connection with the aforementioned matters, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as to ensure legal certainty in the implementation of women’s empowerment and the protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of women and/or children. 33. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 34. Child-Friendly Regency is a regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, society, business world, and media that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights and special protection of children. 35. Private Sector is Non-Governmental Institutions, Business World and Mass Media.

Article 33

(2) Repatriation and social reintegration services for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out after socialization related to the rights of women and children as victims of violence.
(3) Repatriation and social reintegration services as referred to in paragraph (2) are carried out by the Regional Government in coordination with regional apparatus/related institutions, and the community.

Article 56
(1) Regional Government may establish partnerships with the Business Sector in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are conducted through:

b. education and training for Women and Child Victims of Acts of Violence.

I. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural, and the social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as an integral part of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens through various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women’s empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected that they will be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen forms of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.
Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, the community, and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when there is potential violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The said efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.
In connection with the aforementioned matters, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as to ensure legal certainty in the implementation of women’s empowerment and the protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural, and the social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as an integral part of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens through various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women’s empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected that they will be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen forms of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.
Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, the community, and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when there is potential violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The said efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.
In connection with the aforementioned matters, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as to ensure legal certainty in the implementation of women’s empowerment and the protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural, and the social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as an integral part of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens through various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. The said efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

I. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural, and the social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as an integral part of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens through various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women’s empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected that they will be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen forms of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.
Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, the community, and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when there is potential violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The said efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.
In connection with the aforementioned matters, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as to ensure legal certainty in the implementation of women’s empowerment and the protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

Article 25
(1) The Regional Government may establish a PPA Task Force in an effort to coordinate the provision of services for Women and Children who are victims of acts of violence.
(2) The PPA Task Force as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to:
   a. coordinate and synchronize protection services for women and children carried out by the Regional Government, Regional Apparatus/Institutions, and the community;
   b. improve cooperation and referral systems; and collect, compile, and present reports on violence.
(3) The establishment of the PPA Task Force as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be stipulated by Regent's Decree.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
Region is Dompu Regency. 1. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of Regional autonomy. 2. Regent is the Regent of Dompu. 3. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Dompu Regency. 4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the region. 5. Office hereinafter referred to as PPPA Office is the Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Dompu Regency. 6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old, including a child who is still in the womb. 7. Woman is a person who is female in gender. 8. Violence is any act against the physical and psychological aspects that is unlawful, with or without using means, that endangers life or the body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 9. Violence Against Women is any Action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, or psychologically, economic exploitation, social, including threats of certain Actions, coercion, or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 10. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, social, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 11. Domestic violence is any Action or act against a person especially women that results in misery or neglect of the household including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 12. Criminal Act of Sexual Violence hereinafter abbreviated as TPKS is any act that meets the elements of a criminal act as regulated in the Law on Criminal Acts of Sexual Violence and other sexual acts regulated in the Law as long as determined in the Law on Criminal Acts of Sexual Violence. 13. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecution, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 14. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 16. Companion is a person or representative from an Institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy, advocacy, reintegration for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 17. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering either physical, mental or emotional, economic loss either physical suffering, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights as a result of human rights violations or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or individuals including the victim's heirs. 18. Prevention is an effort made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 19. Outreach is an action to respond to reports of alleged problems of women and children that need to be verified and followed up. 20. Social rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to be able to carry out social functions properly in community life. 21. Coordination is an effort made to realize integration and harmony in the context of services for women and children experiencing problems. 22. Task Force for Handling Women's and Children's Problems hereinafter abbreviated as Satgas PPA is a task force formed to handle women's and children's problems reported to women's and children's service organizations that have been established by the regional government. 23. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Women's and Children's Protection hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a Regional Technical Implementation Unit established by the Regional Government in providing Services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems. 24. Regional Child Protection Commission hereinafter abbreviated as KPAD is an independent Institution established by the Regent to support supervision of the implementation of child protection in the region. 25. Integrated Community-Based Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as PATBM is a movement of networks or groups of citizens at the community level who work in a coordinated manner to achieve the goals of child protection. 26. Regional Long-Term Development Plan hereinafter referred to as RPJPD is a regional planning document for a period of 20 (twenty) years. 27. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan hereinafter referred to as RPJMD is a regional planning document for a period of 5 (five) years. 28. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Human Trafficking is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating efforts to prevent and handle criminal acts of human trafficking in Dompu Regency. 29. Task Force for Prevention of Child Marriage is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating efforts to prevent child marriage in Dompu Regency. 30.
